title: Chandratal Lake Travel Guide – The Moon Lake of Himachal Pradesh
content:
Chandratal Lake - Himachal Pradesh, 

Chandratal Lake, often called the “Moon Lake”, is one of the most stunning natural wonders of the Spiti region in Himachal Pradesh. Located at an altitude of about 4,300 meters (14,100 feet), this crescent - shaped lake is surrounded by towering Himalayan peaks and wide meadows that bloom with wildflowers during summer. It is one of the most visited attractions in Spiti, famous among trekkers, campers, and photographers.

The name Chandratal literally means “Lake of the Moon,” inspired by its crescent-like shape. From a distance, the lake changes color with the sunlight - appearing deep blue, turquoise, or greenish at different times of the day. The surrounding landscape is equally enchanting, with snow-clad peaks reflecting in the crystal - clear waters. This makes Chandratal a dream destination for travelers looking to experience the untouched beauty of the Himalayas.

The lake also holds religious and mythological importance. According to local beliefs, it is the spot where Lord Indra’s chariot picked up Yudhishthira, the eldest Pandava, to ascend to heaven. Because of this legend, the lake is considered sacred, and visitors often walk around it as an act of reverence.

Adventure lovers are drawn to Chandratal for its trekking and camping opportunities. The most popular trekking route begins from Batal and continues along rugged paths, crossing streams and rocky terrain, before opening into the mesmerizing meadow near the lake. Another route connects Chandratal to Baralacha La Pass, making it a favorite among seasoned trekkers. For those not keen on long treks, vehicles can reach within a short walking distance from the lake, especially in summer months.

Camping at Chandratal is one of the highlights of visiting the region. As the night falls, the skies light up with millions of stars and the Milky Way galaxy, creating an unforgettable experience. The crisp mountain air, silence broken only by the wind, and the shimmering lake under moonlight make it a place that feels truly magical.

Wildlife and natural diversity also make Chandratal unique. The meadows around the lake are home to rare Himalayan flora and fauna. It is not uncommon to spot blue sheep, Himalayan ibex, or even the elusive snow leopard in the broader Spiti region. Bird watchers may also catch sight of migratory species, including the ruddy shelduck.

Reaching Chandratal is an adventure in itself. The lake is located about 14 km off the Kunzum Pass road, accessible via Batal or Kaza. The roads are narrow, rocky, and often cut through streams, requiring skilled driving. However, the journey rewards travelers with breathtaking views of glaciers, mountains, and valleys at every turn.

In essence, Chandratal Lake is more than just a high-altitude water body - it is an experience of spiritual calm, natural grandeur, and adventure. For trekkers, photographers, nature lovers, and spiritual seekers alike, it remains one of the must-visit destinations in Himachal Pradesh.

How to Reach Chandratal Lake:

Reaching Chandratal Lake is an adventure in itself. The lake is located about 14 km off the Kunzum Pass road and can be accessed from both Manali and Shimla–Kaza routes. Roads are narrow, rocky, and often cut by streams, so traveling requires patience and skilled driving.

  • By Road: The most popular route is via Manali - Rohtang Pass - Gramphu - Batal - Chandratal. From Batal, a dirt road leads towards the lake, ending around 1 - 2 km before, where vehicles must stop. From there, visitors walk to the lake.
  • By Trek: Trekkers can reach Chandratal from Batal (approx. 4 - 5 hours) or connect through the Baralacha La Pass trek.
  • By Bus/Shared Taxi: Public buses run between Manali and Kaza, but they don’t go directly to Chandratal. One must hire a cab or shared jeep from Kaza or Batal.
  • Nearest Airport: Bhuntar Airport (near Kullu), about 250 km from Manali.
  • Nearest Railway Station: Joginder Nagar Railway Station, around 360 km from Manali.

Distance from Major Cities:

  • Manali to Chandratal Lake: 125 km (via Rohtang Pass and Batal).
  • Shimla to Chandratal Lake: 430 km (via Reckong Peo and Kaza).
  • Delhi to Chandratal Lake: 750 km (via Manali).
  • Chandigarh to Chandratal Lake: 550 km (via Manali).
  • Kaza to Chandratal Lake: 50 km (via Kunzum Pass).

Things to Do at Chandratal Lake:

  • Trekking routes from Batal, Kunzum Pass, and Baralacha La.
  • Camping under the stars near the lake.
  • Photography of changing colors of the lake and surrounding peaks.
  • Wildlife spotting: Himalayan ibex, blue sheep, migratory birds.
  • Walking around the lake as part of local religious tradition.
  • Stargazing and astrophotography at night.

Best Time to Visit Chandratal Lake:

  • Peak Season (June - September): Snow melts, roads open, ideal for camping and trekking. Average temperature: 12°C - 20°C.
  • Moderate Season (May & October): Cold weather, occasional snow, fewer tourists. Average temperature: 5°C - 15°C.
  • Low Season (November - April): Roads blocked by heavy snow, lake inaccessible. Temperature:  -5°C to -20°C.

Top 5 Attractions Near Chandratal Lake (within 50 km):

1- Kunzum Pass - High mountain pass offering panoramic Himalayan views.

2- Batal Village - Small settlement known as the gateway to Chandratal.

3- Key Monastery - Iconic Buddhist monastery near Kaza.

4- Dhankar Monastery - Ancient monastery perched on a cliff.

5- Pin Valley National Park - Wildlife and alpine landscapes.
excerpt: Chandratal Lake, the Moon Lake of Himachal Pradesh, is a high-altitude wonder in Spiti Valley known for trekking, camping, and breathtaking views. Surrounded by peaks and meadows, it’s one of the most enchanting Himalayan destinations.
